concerns.text: The plan only validates `alloys_features.csv` against `contracts/alloy_entry.schema.yaml`. It never validates the engineered descriptor file (`CompositionDescriptor`) or any model‑output artifacts against the corresponding schemas (`contracts/composition_descriptor.schema.yaml`, `contracts/model_output.schema.yaml`, `contracts/model_result.schema.yaml`). This leaves the pipeline without enforced schema compliance for two major data products.

The `ModelResult` entity in `data-model.md` includes fields (`sc006_status`, `data_scarcity_warning`, `interpretation_disclaimer`, `microstructure_note`, `residual_confounding_check`) that are **not** present in the `contracts/model_output.schema.yaml` schema, and conversely the contract schema defines fields (`notes`) that the data model does not list. This mismatch means the plan cannot reliably serialize/deserialize model results according to a single source of truth.

A second contract (`model_result.schema.yaml`) defines a substantially different structure (model_id, hyperparameters, metrics sub‑object, validation sub‑object, etc.) that does not align with the `ModelResult` entity in the data model. The plan does not specify which schema will be used, creating ambiguity and violating the Constitution’s Single Source of Truth principle.
